sentence: Clear the cut brush along the back fence and trim the young shrubs planted there.

observation.model_notes: No gate or path into the yard is visible in either photo, so side-yard access could not be assessed. The bed may extend beyond the frame in both directions along the fence line; only what's visible was counted. Cut-brush volume and haul-away needs are not estimated here per instructions.

supporting_evidence.note: Larger, denser pile of cut sticks/brush at the base of the fence-line bed, near the marker pole

evidence.note: Pile of cut brush/sticks sitting on bare soil between two of the young shrubs along the fence
Several cut log rounds/wood pieces lying at the near end of the bed

counting_evidence.note: Wide shot shows three distinct young shrubs planted in a row along the fence bed

supporting_evidence.note: Closer view of two of the same shrubs (matching the ones right of the marker pole in photo 1), showing leaf/branch detail

evidence.note: Three young, thin shrubs staked/caged in bare soil along the fence, roughly waist to shoulder height

service_lines.uncertain: The shrubs appear young with light, open growth and no obviously overgrown or crossing branches in these photos, so it's hard to judge from the images alone how much trimming they need.
